title: Helping hand sheet
subject: PSHE
source: Written for pshe/y3 lesson 3 (Helping hand sheet (pupil PDF))
intro: Lesson 3: Keeping safe at home and online; trusted adults. Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

blocks.title: Sort into: Safe / Ask a grown-up first
blocks.task: sort them into the columns: Safe, Ask a grown-up first.
blocks.answer: Safe: Drinking water; Reading a book. Ask a grown-up first: Taking medicine; Using the kettle; Bleach bottle; Plugging in a charger

panels.title: Safe online
points: Only use school accounts for lessons

box.title: Draw round your hand. On each finger, write one trusted adult. On the palm, write: I can tell.

keywords.def: a grown-up who keeps you safe and listens

questions.q: Is it safe to tell a game player your school's name?

questions.a: For example: my mum and my teacher.

questions.q: Core: Draw a 'helping hand' outline of your own hand and write a trusted adult on each finger (pupil PDF).
Extend: Write three online safety rules for our Teams lessons.
questions.a: For example: first name only; chat for learning; never share a password.

questions.q: Stretch: Explain what you would do if something online made you feel worried, and why.
questions.a: Stop, do not reply, tell a trusted adult, because they can help keep me safe.

questions.q: Someone you do not know messages you in a game. What do you do?
options: Do not reply and tell a trusted adult
questions.a: B) Do not reply and tell a trusted adult. Strangers online may not be who they say; a trusted adult helps you stay safe.

questions.q: A pop-up offers free coins. You should... A) click it B) not click and tell an adult C) give your password
questions.a: B) not click and tell an adult
options: Not click and tell an adult

questions.q: Big question: who are your trusted adults?
questions.a: For example: parents, grandparents and my teacher.
